Subject: Mutual Action Plan & Next Steps — Redwood POC (Acme)

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call today. Thought I’d capture the key pain points, goals, and a suggested mutual action plan so we’re all aligned. I kept this intentionally short; attaching a first-pass MAP and a high-level POC scope (attachments listed below).

Recap / Pain & Goals:
- Pain: unpredictable inference costs and latency spikes during peak scheduling workloads; current infra is overprovisioned for tail latency.
- Goal: 1) Reduce per-token cost ~30% for the scheduling microservice, 2) Achieve p95 latency < 350ms for 512-token calls, 3) Run a 4-week POC with production-like traffic.

Key stakeholders we heard today:
- Sara Thompson — Product (decision lead)
- Tom Lee — ML Engineering (technical evaluation)
- Procurement (contracting) — TBD contact

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (high level):
1) Sign NDA & SOW draft — Owner: Acme Procurement & Redwood Legal — Target: 2027-05-16
2) Technical kickoff + data-preview — Owner: Tom Lee & Redwood SEs (Rafael) — Target: 2027-05-20
3) POC setup (sandbox infra, model pinning, perf baselines) — Owner: Redwood Infra Team (Marcus) & Acme ML Eng — Target: 2027-05-27
4) 2-week ramp + 2-week steady-state eval — Owner: Acme ML Eng / Redwood Ops — Target window: 2027-06-01 to 2027-06-28
5) Post-POC review & commercial decision — Owner: Sara Thompson & Redwood AE (Marissa) — Target: 2027-07-05

Risks / open questions:
- Data residency: you mentioned EU-only data for some customers — confirm scope for the POC (sample traffic vs. customer data).
- Expected throughput: can you confirm concurrency and average tokens per request for the scheduling endpoint?

Attachments:
- acme_map_v1.xlsx (MAP: milestones, owners, sign-off criteria)
- redwood_poc_scope.pdf (POC scope & baseline test plan)

Next steps I’m proposing now:
- I’ll drop the MAP and scope into the thread (attached).
- If you’re good with dates above, can you confirm procurement contact and availability for the 05/20 kickoff?

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and MAP, really helpful. Quick notes from our side after internal sync:

1) Procurement contact: procurement@acme.com (cc'ing generic procurement here for visibility). They prefer an initial SOW and a one-page security addendum before a pilot.
2) Dates: 05/20 kickoff works for Tom and me; procurement asked if we can shift the SOW signing target to 2027-05-18 to give legal a buffer. Is that feasible?
3) Data residency: for the POC we'll use anonymized US traffic; EU-only will not be included in this pilot. We'll confirm sample payloads before the kickoff.
4) Throughput: scheduling endpoint typically sees 120 concurrent requests during peak; average prompt ~280 tokens, response ~140 tokens.

Also added one ask from Tom: can Redwood provide a short list of 3 recommended model/quantization configs you’d evaluate for the POC? Helpful for our capacity planning.

If you can revise the MAP with the procurement contact and the SOW date (05/18), we’ll be able to move procurement quickly.

Appreciate it — Sara
